minutes.headline: Committee agreed it is near settling on the hybrid concept and will build a phased road map with rough costs for the Select Board.
minutes.summary: The committee regrouped after a long gap, recapping the Building Commissioner's code feedback (the 50 percent threshold, change of use, energy code, historic relief) and discussing the hybrid concept for Town Hall, the Ritter building, TC Passios and the Brooks house. Members debated school office/ACE space in the Ritter, tax-assessment uncertainty and the public's appetite for spending, and agreed to work on a phased road map and package the work for the Select Board. A resident asked that Town Hall be described as a possible community space; the meeting adjourned by roll call.

what_happened.line: The committee agreed it has largely met its mission and should finalize and package its concept to present to the Select Board.
The Chair set the next task as working on a phased road map, with rough costs, to take to the town.
Members discussed the hybrid concept for Town Hall, the Ritter building, TC Passios and the Brooks house, including school office space in the Ritter; no change was decided.
The committee recapped the Building Commissioner's code feedback, including the 50 percent threshold, change of use, energy code and historic relief.
The next meeting was set for April 3 by Zoom, with April 11 held for the Select Board; approval of prior minutes was deferred.

why_it_matters: The committee is moving from studying to packaging a phased plan for Town Hall and nearby buildings, so a Select Board discussion of costs and phasing is likely to follow, and any borrowing would reach residents as a vote and a tax bill.

Members raised the cost of the single-building option, borrowing rates, the tax burden on fixed-income residents and uncertainty over the tax assessment, so how the work is phased may decide what a future request asks of taxpayers.
